title: Beza, du Moulin, Faius: fiducia differs from faith as effect from cause
source_text: XLIV. Eadem fuit sententia Bezae, qui scribens in locum Pauli Ephes. 3. In quo libertatem habemus cum fiducia per fidem ipsius; inde colligit fiduciam a fide, ut effectum a causa differre. Ex hoc loco, inquit, apparet manifeste fiduciam a fide, ut effectum a causa differre, ac proinde a nonnullis perperam pro fide substitui nomen fiduciae, quamvis ista duo semper cohaereant. Idem quoque docet Petrus Molinaeus, Disputatione secunda, de Justificatione & fide justificante, Thesi 19. & sequentibus. Censemus, inquit, aliud esse fidem, aliud fiduciam, & hanc esse illius fructum & effectum inseparabilem. Quibus accedit Antonius Fayus, in Thesibus Genevae disputatis, Thesi 20. Libertas, inquit, per quam facilis patet ad Deum accessus, & fiducia per quam clamamus Abba Pater, sunt effecta fidei.
pass_a_gloss: The same was the opinion of Beza, who writing on Paul's place Ephesians 3 — In whom we have liberty with trust through faith in Him — thence gathers that trust differs from faith as effect from cause. From this place, he says, it plainly appears that trust differs from faith as effect from cause, and therefore that by some the name of trust is wrongly substituted for faith, although those two always cohere. The same also Peter du Moulin teaches in the second Disputation on Justification and justifying faith, Thesis 19 and following. We judge, he says, that faith is one thing, trust another, and that this is its fruit and inseparable effect. To whom agrees Anthony Faius in the Theses disputed at Geneva, Thesis 20. Liberty, he says, by which easy access to God lies open, and trust by which we cry Abba Father, are effects of faith.
pass_b_english: Beza on Eph. 3: fiducia differs from faith as effect from cause — do not swap the names.
Du Moulin: faith ≠ fiducia; fiducia = inseparable fruit/effect.
Faius (Geneva): liberty of access and Abba-cry fiducia are effects of faith.
